### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, touching **9** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via os verify (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/verify.ts))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via os verify (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/verify.ts))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **26** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 13a24ece2d005a49dcf4fbf00da62e75ab8a44a0` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1d60401d1a15057ca031bed2f1162fd22a793b10` — the merge of head `d3e368d5ea9979df5e6bfb2546a0d9edc29b3655` into base `13a24ece2d005a49dcf4fbf00da62e75ab8a44a0`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1d60401d1a15057ca031bed2f1162fd22a793b10 && git checkout 1d60401d1a15057ca031bed2f1162fd22a793b10
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 13a24ece2d005a49dcf4fbf00da62e75ab8a44a0 d3e368d5ea9979df5e6bfb2546a0d9edc29b3655 && git checkout -B drift-repro 13a24ece2d005a49dcf4fbf00da62e75ab8a44a0 && git merge --no-ff d3e368d5ea9979df5e6bfb2546a0d9edc29b3655

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 13a24ece2d005a49dcf4fbf00da62e75ab8a44a0
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 13a24ece2d005a49dcf4fbf00da62e75ab8a44a0` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d3e368d5ea9979df5e6bfb2546a0d9edc29b3655`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #21323 (body; comments `5945878976` ruling, `5946405646` claim, `5947667621` os-dev-report), PR #21364 (body, 6-file list, net diff `6c5bef5f4e..refs/review/pr-21364`), `validate.ts` / `compile.ts` / `authoring-rules.ts` / `normalizeStackInput` / `lowerCallables` / `refuseUnbuiltStack` / `loadConfig` / `emitJson` / `packages/verify` at the merge base, the four pins at the merge base, the check-runs on the head.

### ① Derived judgments

**(a) The route against the ruling, step for step.** The util `judgeAuthorTimeRules` (`packages/cli/src/utils/author-time-rules.ts`) against `validate.ts` at `6c5bef5f4e`:

| step | `validate.ts` (merge base) | util at the head | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| normalize | `normalizeStackInput(config, { onConversionNotice })` L273 | `normalizeStackInput(config)` | **right** — `NormalizeStackInputOptions` steers only `convert` (default on) and the notice sink (`spec/src/shared/metadata-collection.zod.ts`); the returned stack is identical. The dropped notices are advisories validate carries under `conversions` / gates with `--strict`, outside the rule verdict |
| lowering | `lowerCallables(normalized)` before the parse L340 | same, same order | **right** — shallow-clone, never mutates its input (`lower-callables.ts` L180, L334), so the `config` verify later boots is the one it loaded |
| parse | `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema.safeParse(lowering.lowered)` L341; failure exits with `errors: issues` | same; failure is `{ stage: 'schema', error }`, verify emits `errors = issues` | **right** |
| manifest beside the config | `resolveJsxGateManifest(result.data, dirname(absolutePath))` L513 | `resolveJsxGateManifest(parsed, configDir)`, verify passes `dirname(absolutePath)` | **right** — an unusable project manifest throws on both: validate's catch-all exits 1; verify's `run()` catch-all exits 1 (`{ error }` under `--json`) |
| union fold + filter judge + lowered hook refs | `authoringRuleUnionStack(result.data)`, `stackFilterJudge(parsedUnion)`, `runAuthoringRules('validate', { normalized: authoringRuleUnionStack(normalized), parsed: parsedUnion, sduiManifest, loweredHookRefs: lowering.loweredHookRefs, judgeFilter })`, `splitBySeverity` L516-531 | the same five members, same functions | **right** |
| per-package pass + skip | `artifactPackages(result.data).length` above zero → `runPerPackageAuthoringRules({ command: 'validate', parsed: result.data, unionFindings: findings, sduiManifest, loweredHookRefs, judgeFilter })`; errors refuse, advisories fold L601-636 | `artifactPackages(parsed).length === 0` → pass; else the same call with the same six members | **right** — identical skip condition |
| door | `authoringRulesFor('validate')` / `runAuthoringRules('validate', …)` | `VERIFY_RULE_COMMAND = 'validate'` | **right** — `runAuthoringRules` only filters by `r.commands.includes(command)` (`authoring-rules.ts`), and `authoring-rule-wiring.test.ts` pins the gating set identical across the three doors, so `'validate'` is parity by construction and `'build'` would differ only in advisories |

No step exists at which the util's rule verdict can diverge from `os validate`'s rule verdict on the same stack: the inputs, functions and order are validate's, and the rule roster is `authoringRulesFor(command)` from the one table — no second rule set (ruling `5945878976`). What the util deliberately does not run is everything `validate.ts` wires AROUND the rule stage: 1a `refuseUnbuiltStack` (the `defineStack` provenance refusal, #20367 ruling B — also `compile.ts` L279), 2c `findViewContainerNameRefusals`, 2d `judgePicklistReferences`, 3b capability preflight, 3c package docs, and `--strict`. On a stack one of those refuses, `os validate` exits 1 and `os verify` can reach the runtime stage; on a stack that trips 2c/2d AND a rule, both exit 1 with different `errors` (validate's 2c/2d exit precedes its rule run). That is a boundary of the stage (③.2), not a divergence of the rule verdict.

**(b) The four pins are real constraints at the merge base**, each scanning only `validate.ts` / `compile.ts` / `lint.ts` source text: `packages/lint/src/authoring-rule-wiring.test.ts` L250-252 (`it.each(AUTHORING_COMMANDS)`: each door's file must match `/\brunAuthoringRules\s*\(/`); `packages/cli/test/validate-build-gate-parity.test.ts` L712-716 (`calls(file, 'runAuthoringRules')` for `compile.ts` and `validate.ts`), L737-760 with `handsFoldedStack` L692-709 (the in-file `runAuthoringRules(` call's `normalized`/`parsed` tier expressions must resolve through `const` bindings in the same file to a literal `authoringRuleUnionStack(`), L859-890 (every bare-identifier call site in the two files must sit in a ledger — a `judgeAuthorTimeRules(` call there is unclassified until a row is added), L1109-1121 (each door passes an `onConversionNotice` sink); `packages/cli/test/lint-per-package-authoring-seam.test.ts` L55, L179-185 (each door must match `/\brunPerPackageAuthoringRules\s*\(/`); `packages/cli/src/utils/sdui-manifest.test.ts` L498-512 (each door has exactly one `resolveJsxGateManifest(` call and the same count of `dirname(absolutePath)`). Lifting the stage out of `validate.ts` / `compile.ts` moves exactly the text these read — **the dev's claim is right**, and one of the four is in `@objectstack/lint`, off the claim's file surface.

**(c) Behaviour pins.** `packages/cli/test/verify-author-time-stage.test.ts` **does** compare: on the card's three planted mistakes (lookup to `vg_projects`, `visible: 'done != true'`, column `{ field: 'priority' }`) it runs `os validate --json`, requires exit 1 and the rule list `['expression-invalid','object-reference-unknown','list-view-field-unknown']` as a positive control, then runs `os verify --json`, requires exit 1, ONE parseable document, and `expect(verifyDoc.errors).toEqual(validateDoc.errors)` (L151-167); the text face must exit 1, name each `rule: …`, contain `the runtime stage did not run` and not the runtime header (L169-177); the clean control must exit 0 with `Author-time rules passed` and the runtime header `=== objectstack verify` (`packages/verify/src/verify.ts` L140) (L179-186). It goes red on any drift that changes the gating findings on that stack, on a boot before the stage, and on a stage that refuses everything. Its blind spot is drift that leaves those three findings intact (a new rule-context input added at validate's call only). `packages/cli/src/utils/author-time-rules.test.ts` pins the door (`VERIFY_RULE_COMMAND === 'validate'`), the union fold (an option-B stack with definitions only in `packages[]` is refused at `stage: 'rules'` with `object-reference-unknown` at `objects[0].fields.ghost.reference`; the corrected control passes), the per-package pass (a two-package artifact where `field-no-consumers` on `industry` reaches `advisories` under the `package '…' — ` prefix and is absent from the union run), and the schema refusal (`stage: 'schema'`, at least one issue). **Right on all four** — with the note that the per-package seam is pinned through an advisory, so the `stage: 'package-rules'` refusal branch of the util and verify's third sentence are not themselves exercised by any pin. The spawned pin runs through `TSX` + `bin/run-dev.js` like the four other TSX-spawned pins at the base; the dev's red-before / ablation readings are the dev's; the green is the check-runs below.

**(d) Docs (`cli.mdx`, `### Quality` only — the diff's two hunks sit at L1614-1620 and L1683-1738, inside `### Quality` L1612-1738) and changeset, sentence by sentence against the head:** two stages in order, the second only after the first — right (`runAuthorTimeStage` before `bootStack`, exits inside on refusal). Stage 1 prepared as validate prepares it, judged whole then per package, a non-parsing or gating-refused stack fails with validate's findings and never boots — right. Advisories never fail; the text face counts them and validate prints them — right (`advisory finding(s) — os validate prints them`; validate L841-843, `printJsxGateNotices`). "This stage is the rule registry, not all of os validate: package-docs, capability-provider, picklist-reference and view-container-name checks and `--strict` stay validate's, so run it too" — true for every item named, **incomplete by one**: the `defineStack` provenance refusal (`refuseUnbuiltStack`, validate 1a / build 1a) also stays validate's and is not listed (③.2). Runtime stage: per-object create/read/compare with create, read or fidelity failures failing the run — right (`hardFailures` sums `createFailed + readFailed + fidelityGaps`); `--rls` second fresh boot, probe persona plus one persona per declared position, a hole fails — right (`rlsStack`, `declaredPositionNames`, `totals.holes`; degraded probe and `positionCoverage.notRun` also count, undocumented but not contradicted); `--multi-tenant` boots org-scoped, and `OS_TENANCY_POSTURE` `isolated`/`group` asks for the same boot — right (`resolveVerifyMultiTenant` = flag OR `postureEnforcesWall(resolveTenancyPosture())`; `TENANCY_POSTURES = ['single','group','isolated']`, wall = `!== 'single'`; `bootStack({ multiTenant })` mounts `@objectstack/organizations` and requests `isolated`). Exit table: `0` both stages, `1` stage-1 refusal / runtime failures / could not run — right (`this.exit(1)` in the stage, `this.exit(1)` when `hardFailures` is above zero else `this.exit(0)`, catch-all `exit(1)`); oclif's own parse-error exit is outside the table, as in the neighbouring entries. `--json` shapes: refusal `{ error, errors }` with validate's finding shape (`package` on per-package, Zod issues on schema) — right (`emitJson({ error: sentence, errors }, 0, { compact: true })`); runtime report `app, config, multiTenant, crud, rls (with --rls), hardFailures` — right (verify L267; `rls` undefined is dropped by `JSON.stringify`); could-not-run `{ error }` plus `code`/`httpStatus` when carried — right (`errorCodeFields`). Changeset: "What was accepted before" / "What is refused now" match the diff; "every stack it [the first stage] refuses, `os build` refuses too" — right by construction: `compile.ts` runs the same normalize → lower → parse (schema refusal at its step 3) → fold → `runAuthoringRules('build', …)` → `runPerPackageAuthoringRules` over the same prepared stack with the gating set pinned identical across doors, and refuses more besides (1a, 3a, 3a-bis, capabilities, docs). Read for `verify` as a whole the sentence would be false (a runtime failure is not a build refusal); the changeset scopes it to the first stage, correctly. The `examples/*` readings are the dev's; the converged `Dogfood Verify CLI` run (`objectstack verify --rls` on `examples/app-crm` and `examples/app-showcase` through the built CLI, `.github/workflows/ci.yml` L1840-1841) is the CI-level clean control on this head.

### ② Semver level

**Right.** `@objectstack/cli` `minor` with a `**BREAKING**` banner and `fix(cli)!:` is the launch-window spelling (`scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` header: breaking ships as `minor`, the banner and the `!` are the carriers); AGENTS.md Post-Task #3: `Clause-②: yes` takes at least `minor`, `(narrowing)` is BREAKING. The narrowing arm is the measured one: `verify` newly exits 1 on a set it passed at the base, and nothing it passed before and passes now is judged differently. The one added `--json` key, `errors`, is an additive output member on an exit that did not exist before, not an accept-set arm; it is declared in the changeset, the PR body and the docs, and `minor` covers it. ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`: nothing authorable moves (no key, export, spelling or stored shape), the body carries no FROM → TO rewrite, and the remedy is the finding `os validate` / `os build` already print for the same stack — the disposition is right, and the gate's own verdict is the converged `Check Changeset` run below — the job that runs `check-changeset-no-major.mjs --base` and `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs --base` (`.github/workflows/pr-automation.yml` L244, L980, L1130). The PR body's line 2 carries the `Clause-②` line the claim prescribed.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Route deviation (dev `deviations[0]`, `open_questions[0]`).** The ruling binds the rule SET ("no second rule set") and the pipeline; the util names no rule, takes the roster from `authoringRulesFor(command)`, and runs validate's functions in validate's order — within the ruling. It is, however, a fourth hand-wiring of that pipeline, the class the four source-scan pins were written against (#3782, #4409, #17069, #18677, #16544 all drifted at a door's wiring), and the util sits outside all four scans. The behaviour pins cover the drift classes that have occurred; the uncovered residual is a future member added to validate's `runAuthoringRules` call (the #16546 `loweredHookRefs` / #20158 `judgeFilter` class) that the planted fixture does not trip. Answered for this landing: **accepted**, on the measured pin constraint, the off-surface `packages/lint` pin, and the two new pins. Open question 1 **escalated to the PM**: B is right for this PR; a follow-up card is warranted and cheap in one of two shapes — the dev's A (retarget the four pins to the util, lift the doors onto it), or narrower, a source-parity pin in `packages/cli` holding the util's `runAuthoringRules(` / `runPerPackageAuthoringRules(` member lists equal to `validate.ts`'s. C (export from `validate.ts`) needs a NOT_A_GATE row and hooks and buys less than either.
2. **Stage-1 scope (dev `open_questions[1]`).** Within the ruling's text ("the author-time rules … through the same pipeline os validate uses"). Against the card's Expected it lands between the two branches: "verify green ⇒ validate green" holds for validate's rule stage (schema + registry + per-package), not for 1a provenance, 2c view-container (refused by `os serve` at boot anyway), 2d picklist, 3b capability provider, 3c package docs or `--strict`; the pass line does not state what it skipped, the docs do and say to run `os validate` too. Five of those six are disclosed in the docs sentence, the PR's acceptance notes and the report; **the `defineStack` provenance refusal is not** — a plain-object export that `os validate` and `os build` refuse at exit 1 (`STACK_PROVENANCE_MISSING`) now has its rules judged by `os verify` and, when they pass, boots. The docs sentence is true as written and the remedy it gives ("run it too") covers the omitted case, so this is not blocking; it is a one-clause amendment to that sentence (name the provenance refusal) and the same addition to the triage-visible list — on this PR before landing if the dev is still on it, otherwise on the follow-up. Widening stage 1 (the dev's B) is a second ruling: **escalated to the maintainer through the PM**, with the reviewer's reading that the triage title ("`verify` cannot pass a stack the build refuses") states the intent more widely than the ruling's mechanism delivers, so the question is a real one.
3. **`out_of_scope_findings`.** (i) carrier #21308 — consistent with the base's own `serve-process.ts` (`RUN_JS_RESOLVES_FROM_DIST`, `requireBuiltCli`); the new pin spawns through `TSX` like the four other TSX-spawned pins at the base; nothing to file. (ii) carrier #21324 — the claim excluded it; a stage-1 refusal is one document (pinned), the runtime-stage report is byte-unchanged, so #21324's scope is unchanged. (iii) carrier none — a `**Options.**` table for `os verify` needs a GOVERNED row in `docs-cli-enumeration-parity.test.ts`; Prime Directive 10 files an issue for a defect, a contract violation or a trap, and an absent optional table is none, so a PR note is the right carrier.
4. **Other dev deviations.** Options table omitted — right (the pin governs it). Repro control re-measured at `222ecc27f9` — the dev's reading. Pin spawned via tsx not node — right (helper convention). Merge commit `5d0486c67d` with git's default message — `check:commit-card-trailers` is in the gate set; the check-runs are the verdict. PM probe answered with one SendMessage — no GitHub write; `mcp_calls: 0`, `api_writes: 3` all through `scripts/pm`.
5. **`Fixes #21323` — right.** The card's two asks are both closed and pinned: `verify` fails on the three planted mistakes with validate's findings and exit 1 (and the clean stack passes), and `#### os verify` under `### Quality` states the two stages, the exit mapping and `--json`. `The card this PR closes must claim this branch` and `Part-of PR must not also close its card` are green; closing the card on merge is correct. `packages/cli/README.md` carries no `os verify` row at the base (#21310's surface untouched); no governed path in the six files (`Governed Surface Queue Guard` green).
6. **Check-runs on `d3e368d5ea`, collapsed latest-per-name, converged (read 2026-10-02T08:07:19Z; 19 were in progress and 1 queued at dispatch):** 35 names — 33 `success`, 2 `skipped`, 0 failed, none still running.
